scope: Corollary 4.9 (Transverse crossings) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a Jordan quadrilateral in a reference chart. Prescribe one crossing between its first and third sides and another between its second and fourth sides, with endpoint ports beyond those sides, and with positive clearance from the inappropriate sides. Discrete surface paths satisfying sufficiently accurate versions of these requirements intersect. If both are primal graph walks, they have a common primal vertex. The assertion holds simultaneously for every fixed finite collection of such strict tests, on the sphere or in a protected bilateral window.
